arxiv-2103-02956.title: Magnetic fields and Star Formation around H ii regions: The S235 complex Journal: ApJ
arxiv-2103-02956.creator: Devaraj R, D.P. Clemens, L.K. Dewangan, A. Luna, T.P. Ray, J. Mackey
arxiv-2103-02956.description: Abstract Magnetic fields are ubiquitous and essential in star formation. In particular, their role in regulating formation of stars across diverse environments like H ii regions needs to be well understood. In this study, we present magnetic field properties towards the S235 complex using near-infrared (NIR) H H -band polarimetric observations, obtained with the Mimir and POLICAN instruments.

arxiv-2203-02968.title: Improved Quantum Query Upper Bounds Based on Classical Decision Trees An extended abstract of this work appeared in the proceedings of FSTTCS 2022 [ CMP22 ] .
arxiv-2203-02968.creator: Arjan Cornelissen, Nikhil S. Mande, Subhasree Patro
arxiv-2203-02968.description: Abstract We consider the following question in query complexity: Given a classical query algorithm in the form of a decision tree, when does there exist a quantum query algorithm with a speed-up (i.e., that makes fewer queries) over the classical one?

arxiv-2209-14778.title: Batch Normalization Explained
arxiv-2209-14778.creator: Randall Balestriero, Richard G. Baraniuk
arxiv-2209-14778.description: Abstract A critically important, ubiquitous, and yet poorly understood ingredient in modern deep networks (DNs) is batch normalization (BN), which centers and normalizes the feature maps. To date, only limited progress has been made understanding why BN boosts DN learning and inference performance; work has focused exclusively on showing that BN smooths a DN’s loss landscape.

arxiv-2212-05813.title: KonX: Cross-Resolution Image Quality Assessment
arxiv-2212-05813.creator: Oliver Wiedemann, Vlad Hosu, Shaolin Su, Dietmar Saupe
arxiv-2212-05813.description: Abstract Scale-invariance is an open problem in many computer vision subfields. For example, object labels should remain constant across scales, yet model predictions diverge in many cases. This problem gets harder for tasks where the ground-truth labels change with the presentation scale. In image quality assessment (IQA), down-sampling attenuates impairments, e.g.

arxiv-2307-11873.title: It Is Easy For Multi-Issue Bundles To Advance Anti-Democratic Agendas
arxiv-2307-11873.creator: Matthew I. Jones, Matthew Chervenak, Nicholas A. Christakis
arxiv-2307-11873.description: Abstract Abstract When confronted with a host of issues, groups often save time and energy by compiling many issues into a single bundle when making decisions. This reduces the time and cost of group decision-making, but it also leads to suboptimal outcomes as individuals lose the ability to express their preferences on each specific issue.

arxiv-2404-16995.title: Star-Image Centering with Deep Learning II: HST/WFPC2 Full Field of View Journal: PASP Facilities: HST (WFPC2), MAST
arxiv-2404-16995.creator: Dana I. Casetti-Dinescu, Roberto Baena-Gallé, Terrence M. Girard, Alejandro Cervantes-Rovira, Sebastian Todeasa
arxiv-2404-16995.description: Abstract We present an expanded and improved deep-learning (DL) methodology for determining centers of star images on HST/WFPC2 exposures. Previously, we demonstrated that our DL model can eliminate the pixel-phase bias otherwise present in these undersampled images; however that analysis was limited to the central portion of each detector.

arxiv-2407-20694.title: Detecting Causality in the Frequency Domain with Cross-Mapping Coherence
arxiv-2407-20694.creator: Zsigmond Benkő, Bálint Varga, Marcell Stippinger, Zoltán Somogyvári
arxiv-2407-20694.description: Abstract Understanding causal relationships within a system is crucial for uncovering its underlying mechanisms. Causal discovery methods, which facilitate the construction of such models from time-series data, hold the potential to significantly advance scientific and engineering fields. This study introduces the Cross-Mapping Coherence (CMC) method, designed to reveal causal connections in the frequency domain between time series.

arxiv-2408-06954.title: Neural Speech and Audio Coding
arxiv-2408-06954.creator: Minje Kim
arxiv-2408-06954.description: Abstract Abstract : This paper explores the integration of model-based and data-driven approaches within the realm of neural speech and audio coding systems. It highlights the challenges posed by the subjective evaluation processes of speech and audio codecs and discusses the limitations of purely data-driven approaches, which often require inefficiently large architectures to match the performance of model-based methods.

arxiv-2411-00288.title: Inducing Semi-Structured Sparsity by Masking for Efficient Model Inference in Convolutional Networks
arxiv-2411-00288.creator: David A. Danhofer
arxiv-2411-00288.description: Abstract The crucial role of convolutional models, both as standalone vision models and backbones in foundation models, necessitates effective acceleration techniques. This paper proposes a novel method to learn semi-structured sparsity patterns for convolution kernels in the form of maskings enabling the utilization of readily available hardware accelerations.

arxiv-2508-17166.title: Generative Flow Networks for Personalized Multimedia Systems: A Case Study on Short Video Feeds Conference: Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia; October 27–31, 2025; Dublin, Ireland Proceedings of the 33rd ACM International Conference on Multimedia (MM ’25), October 27
arxiv-2508-17166.creator: Yili Jin, Ling Pan, Rui-Xiao Zhang, Jiangchuan Liu, Xue Liu
arxiv-2508-17166.description: Abstract . Multimedia systems underpin modern digital interactions, facilitating seamless integration and optimization of resources across diverse multimedia applications. To meet growing personalization demands, multimedia systems must efficiently manage competing resource needs, adaptive content, and user-specific data handling. This paper introduces Generative Flow Networks (GFlowNets, GFNs) as a brave new framework for enabling personalized multimedia systems.

pmc-10702274.title: Anesthesia and perioperative management of bariatric surgery in a patient with BMI over 70 kg/m2: a case report
pmc-10702274.creator: Ling Dong, Chunxia Huang, Benli Jia, Ye Zhang, Qi Xue
pmc-10702274.description: The anesthesia protocol of bariatric surgery has not been standardized in detail. This report introduced an optimized anesthesia strategy for a severely obese male patient for laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy and a continuous follow-up for 12 months. A 34-year-old male patient was admitted for super-super-obesity with obstructive sleep apnea-hypopnea syndrome.

pmc-11375509.title: Diagnosis of contralateral rare pulmonary cavity metastasis after lung squamous cell carcinoma surgery by electromagnetic navigation: one case report and review of the literature
pmc-11375509.creator: Zhengjun Li, Xiaoge Wang, Chang Liu, Yi Ren
pmc-11375509.description: BackgroundLung cancer associated with cystic airspaces is a rare disease, and a rare imaging performance of non-small cell lung cancer. Due to the lack of conventional diagnosis methods, it is difficult to rely on imaging diagnosis. Therefore, the definitive diagnosis of these neoplastic lesions remains challenging.

pmc-12450230.title: Methanosarcina acetivorans requires methanol:coenzyme M methyltransferases for ethane formation from ethanol
pmc-12450230.creator: Tejas Somvanshi, Mai Anh Tran, Jichen Bao, Silvan Scheller
pmc-12450230.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Corrinoid-dependent enzymes either catalyze methyltransfer reactions, or they generate substrate radicals using adenosylcobalamin for subsequent rearrangement reactions. The corrinoid-dependent methyltransferases are present in all domains of life and assumed to be exclusive for methyl-groups. In Methanosarcina, however, trace ethane production from ethanol has been shown in vivo, which led to the hypothesis that corrinoid-dependent methanol-specific methyltransferases are promiscuous towards also accepting ethyl-groups.

pmc-12738578.title: Assessing knowledge, attitudes, and barriers toward HPV cervical cancer and vaccination among female university students in Bangladesh
pmc-12738578.creator: Hasibul Hassain Emon, Rawfun Nahin Kowbi, Md Nayeem Chowdhury, Tanha Rasheed Teep, Md Ahashan Habib, Farzana Tayeeba, Md Moyazzem Hossain
pmc-12738578.description: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a leading cause of genital warts and cervical cancer (CC), which was reported as the second most common malignancy among women in Bangladesh in 2020. While vaccination against HPV stands out as the most effective strategy for preventing CC, however, misconceptions about its safety, effectiveness, and benefits may impact its prevalence.

pmc-12971852.title: Soil Microbiome for Climate Smart Agriculture in Legumes: A Review
pmc-12971852.creator: Kusum Raj Tamang, Sakina Mahdi, Prabesh Koirala, Joshua Yeboah Asiamah, Swastika Sharma, Shreesha Padyana, Christian B Carson, Babu Valliyodan
pmc-12971852.description: Climate-smart agriculture is a multidisciplinary farm model approach that helps reduce the impact of climate change not only on soil but on entire agricultural systems. One of the critical approaches of climate-smart agriculture is using the soil microbiome to help the crop adapt to the changing climate and increase crop production.

pmc-12992091.title: Unraveling the influence of TGF-β rs9282871 and miRNA let-7c relative expression on TGF-β production in hepatocellular carcinoma patients
pmc-12992091.creator: Sally Farouk, Maha M. Elbrashy, Ahmed Khairy, Noha G. Bader El Din
pmc-12992091.description: Highlights•TGF-β rs9282871 TT genotype linked to high HCC susceptibility.•Serum TGF-β was markedly elevated in hepatocellular carcinoma patients.•miR-let-7c expression was significantly downregulated in HCC cases.•Inverse correlation between TGF-β levels and miR-let-7c expression.•TGF-β and miR-let-7c serve as potential diagnostic HCC biomarkers. Introduction Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) poses a severe health problem and risk globally.

pmc-13351952.title: Endoscope-assisted prone lateral retropleural 360° reconstruction of thoracic pathological fracture in metastatic melanoma: a case report and technical note
pmc-13351952.creator: Fidel Toomey, Mendel Castle-Kirszbaum, Frederick Mariajoseph, Jeremy Kam, Idrees Sher
pmc-13351952.description: BackgroundAdvances in oncological therapies have increased survival rates, however, these may result in more patients developing secondary disease processes, including pathological spinal fractures requiring surgical decompression and stabilisation. Traditional open approaches carry significant morbidity, particularly for thoracic anterior column reconstruction.

pmc-13572795.title: Glomus Tumors of Uncertain Malignant Potential Arising in the Endobronchus and Lung Parenchyma
pmc-13572795.creator: Hao Ma, Fengzhang Zhu, Shizhou Tang, Jiaxin Yin, Xianglin Zhang
pmc-13572795.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Pulmonary glomus tumors are rare, and synchronous endobronchial and pulmonary parenchymal lesions are particularly uncommon. A 72-year-old woman was admitted with a 20-day history of cough and blood-streaked sputum. Contrast-enhanced chest computed tomography demonstrated a 25 × 20 mm solid nodule in the apicoposterior segment of the left upper lobe and a 13 × 8 mm endobronchial nodule in the left upper-lobe bronchus. Both lesions had smooth margins, prominent vascularity, and persistent enhancement.
